key_insight: A single model-based reinforcement learning network can generate robust quantum control pulses across a continuous family of gate settings, learning reusable structure instead of solving each instance from scratch.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, adaptable quantum pulse synthesis for real-time control, reducing optimization cost while maintaining fidelities comparable to multi-seed GRAPE.
method: Embed the Hamiltonian directly into the neural training loop
Use model-based reinforcement learning to output pulses for arbitrary control parameters
Exploit learned symmetry-invariant phase structure for smooth interpolation across gate settings
evidence_signal: On a single-spin two-level system, the trained network produced pulses in milliseconds across varying angles, durations, detunings, and inhomogeneities with fidelities comparable to multi-seed GRAPE.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated on a simplified single-spin system, so scalability and robustness on larger multi-qubit hardware still need validation.
paper_title: Uncovering Latent Structures in Robust Pulse Sequences: A Model-Based Reinforcement Learning Approach for Adaptable Quantum Control
